thread:
sara: Heads-up — we hit a near-OOM on apac-h24 at ~04:12 UTC. GPU nodes in pool-gamma got >95% memory and started throttling requests.

mike: timeline? what triggered the spike?

sara: short version: a long-running streaming job kept appending large KV-cache prefixes, combined with a short autoscaler cooldown. steady 30% traffic rise from a partner burst pushed memory to the edge.

jasmin: can you paste the alloc logs / node OOM traces?

sara: logs (trimmed):
```
[04:09:12] node-gn12: free_mem 2.3GB / total_gpu_mem 24GB
[04:11:03] rtq: prefix_kv_store += 1.4GB per minute
[04:12:08] scheduler: throttle start reason=mem_pressure
[04:12:17] worker-7: eviction_failed reason=locked_stream
```

luis: looks like the prefix/KV caching didn't evict because the stream was pinned. we've seen that edge case in sim before but it wasn't hitting prod due to shorter session lengths.

mike: was the fallback routing triggered (to model-smaller or euw)? capacity-bot what does routing log say?

capacity-bot: routing decision: pool-gamma capacity_exceeded -> attempted fallback to pool-beta (euw1) -> failed (incompatible quantized variant) -> queued requests incremented.

jasmin: so two failure modes: cache eviction didn't free memory and fallback couldn't accept those requests. combination caused throttling rather than graceful degradation.

ops-oncall: immediate mitigation notes: 1) manually evict prefixes on affected nodes (done @04:18), 2) taint pool-gamma to stop new allocations (04:20), 3) spin up extra dedicated nodes in apac (04:22) — those actions recovered latency by ~80% within 12 minutes.

mike: cost hit from emergency spin-up?

luis: extra GPU-hours ~ 7.2 over 3 hours due to warmup / reservation. estimated incremental cost ~ $4.6k.

jasmin: we need a root cause write-up and a set of short fixes: behavioral fixes (prevent pinned-streams from blocking eviction), routing fixes (compat fallback matching on quantization), and forecasting tweaks (simulate long-tail streaming sessions).

sara: quick action items I propose:
- add eviction preempt for pinned streams after 90s idle (sara)
- enhance fallback matcher to allow compatible quantized fallbacks (mike)
- add a scenario to the capacity simulator for sustained streaming prefixes (jasmin)
- review autoscaler cooldown and burst policy for apac pools (luis)

mike: +1. Also add an alert that correlates KV-cache growth rate with free_gpu_mem, so we don't only alert on absolute thresholds.

luis: note on forecasting: our model currently uses 95th percentile session length from the last 7 days — that misses partner bursts that keep sessions alive >24h. We should include a heavy-tail component or run a separate sim for partner-scheduled promos.

ops-oncall: logs and the manual mitigation steps are in the incident runbook: /incidents/1778901234-apac-kv-buildup (internal link). I'll attach the node eviction commands there.

jasmin: follow-ups: can eng-runtime add a non-blocking eviction path this sprint? if not, a temporary guardrail to hard-limit per-session KV prefix size.

sara: engineering action owner assignments: eviction preempt (jasmin), fallback matcher (mike), sim/scenario (jasmin + data), autoscaler param review (luis). I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow.

mike: one more ops improvement: add a pre-warmed cross-region route that accepts lower-precision models for overflow; keep it enabled for high-risk windows. saves on emergency cold starts.

luis: agree, but capture privacy/SLA constraints before enabling cross-region overflow. We'll gate by account tier.

capacity-bot: reminder: incident severity was S2. Auto-summary queued for docs.

sara: thanks all — postmortem draft due EOD + retro meeting in 48h.

mike: quick note: re-run the capacity simulator with a 40% increase in long sessions and 2x prefix growth; screenshot attached in runbook.

jasmin: putting an experiment in place to cap per-session prefix to 3GB as a temporary safety valve.

ops-oncall: closing loop: recovered at 04:30UTC, no customer-facing errors reported. leaving pool-gamma tainted until eviction preempt is deployed.

sara: tl;dr — near-OOM due to pinned streaming KV growth + incompatible fallback; mitigated manually; short-term guardrails and longer-term fixes assigned.

mike: :thumbsup:

luis: tagging finance for the emergency cost: @finance — we'll submit a one-off variance for Q2 infra ops.

finance: acknowledged, please include the runbook link and the GPU-hours estimate.
